title: The Citadel
description: Boss round: estimate, then design a system that uses everything you have learned.

challenges.prompt: 10 million daily active users each make about 10 requests a day. What is the average load?
challenges.explanation: 100 million requests ÷ 86,400 seconds ≈ 1,160 req/s. Peak is usually 2-3× the average, so plan for that.

challenges.prompt: Your SLA promises 99.9% availability. How much downtime is that per year?
challenges.explanation: 0.1% of 8,760 hours ≈ 8.8 hours. Each extra nine divides it by 10: 99.99% is about 53 minutes.

challenges.prompt: Which of these is a single point of failure?
options: Three app servers behind a load balancer
One load balancer with no standby
A database with a promoted replica on standby
A CDN with many edge locations
challenges.explanation: If the only load balancer dies, nothing gets through, however many servers sit behind it. Run load balancers in active-passive pairs.

challenges.prompt: Boss fight: a global launch at 10,000 req/s with a 2× peak, plenty of static media and a steady stream of writes. Use everything in your toolbox.
challenges.explanation: The CDN takes 40% of the 20,000 req/s peak. A cache shields the database from reads, a queue flattens the write spike so 2 shards are enough, and about 12 app servers behind a load balancer handle the rest.
